messages.subject: LOD support interval from find_peaks
parts:
Dear Karl,
I got some strange results for LOD support interval from find_peaks.
For my chr. 1B I found significant peak by loco (permutations gave me 3.25, peak is 3.5).
I used threshold by permutations, peakdrop=1.5 and drop=1.
Find_peaks gave me ci_lo 1.75 cM and ci_hi 156.13 cM, when manual calculation gave me ci_lo 3 cM and ci_hi 18.41 cM.
I tried to change  peakdrop value and also runed without it, but got the same results
Could you please advise me with this problem?
I shared by google drive csv file with LODs of target chr., R script and image of results.

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/16rIBwoRU4cf3HK2W3Xyv7q9YS-uErTjR?usp=sharing

Thank you in advance.

Best regards

Andrii Fatiukha

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: LOD support interval from find_peaks
parts:
It's because of that blip out to the right, which is below the threshold so isn't considered its own peak but is within 1 of the maximum LOD. (see attached figure)

The effort to try to call multiple peaks and get LOD support intervals in this sort of single-dimensional QTL scan is not going to have some imperfections.

karl

messages.subject: Re: LOD support interval from find_peaks
parts: Is it means that all points on line with target drop will be included to support interval does not matter how far they are?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Re: LOD support interval from find_peaks
parts:
Having identified a set of peaks, it then seeks intervals where the LOD score is within drop of the maximum. If there is just one peak on the chromosome, it looks for all positions that are within drop of the maximum, and then takes the full broad interval.

karl
